children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a 17-year-old son, Alex, who lives at home with me. I was wondering if I could claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! 

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation since he's 17 years old.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school anymore. He finished his GCSEs and left education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and has left education, I need to ask:

Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with a careers service or anything like that. He's actually started an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one more detail:

Is Alex's apprenticeship an apprenticeship in England?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's not in England - he's doing his apprenticeship in Northern Ireland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment:

Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week in his apprenticeship in Northern Ireland?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work 24 hours or more per week. It's less than that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also confirm: Do you live in the UK, and is Alex living with you at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Although Alex is 17 and has left education, the specific conditions that would stop Child Benefit don't apply in your situation:

- Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland (the rule about apprenticeships only applies to apprenticeships in England)
- Alex works less than 24 hours per week (Child Benefit only stops if a child works 24 hours or more per week AND is no longer in approved education or training)

Since you live in the UK and Alex lives at home with you, you meet the basic requirements for claiming Child Benefit.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay back some or all of it through tax.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and lives at home with the claimant in the UK. According to the rules, Child Benefit normally qualifies for children under 16, but continues for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. While Alex has left education and is not in approved education, he has started an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland (not England) and works less than 24 hours per week. The rules state that Child Benefit stops if the child 'starts an apprenticeship in England' or 'starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training'. Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland (not England) and he works less than 24 hours per week, neither of these disqualifying conditions apply. Therefore, the claimant remains eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
